- Overestimate prices in the short term after sentiment spikes (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.18) — model fails to anticipate sharp declines.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to recent highs/lows, fails to smoothly transition toward historical mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses early downward momentum, especially after sentiment drops.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.36 and 0.00), model overfits recent noise and fails to adjust for structural shifts.
- Avoid extrapolating upward from recent peaks — sentiment decay often precedes price correction, not continuation.
- If sentiment drops below 0.10, reduce forecast slope — model tends to ignore sentiment signals and overpredicts recovery.
